groups.layman: This child's device lost the sign-in, so the child was shown the sign-in screen again (this is the “keeps signing out” report).
groups.technical: device cookie present but no device record in storage (reason=no matching device record for the cookie that was sent): cookiePresent=true deviceFound=false kidFound=false storage=unknown durable=true location=/home/user/BrainyKids/.data
groups.fix: Attach a permanent database (DATABASE_URL on Vercel) so device links survive a restart, then link the device again. Until then, each new server instance starts from an empty temporary file.

groups.layman: BrainyKids cannot save permanently on this server, so accounts, children and device links can disappear when the server restarts.
groups.technical: file driver not durable: location=/tmp/brainykids-data reason=This server's project folder is read-only, so BrainyKids is keeping accounts in a temporary folder. They can disappear when the server restarts — attach a Neon or Vercel Postgres database (DATABASE_URL) for permanent storage. driver=file
groups.fix: Attach a Neon/Vercel Postgres database (DATABASE_URL) and redeploy. This one change fixes sign-outs and missing children together.

groups.layman: This child's device is no longer linked on the server, so the app returned to the sign-in screen.
groups.technical: heartbeat answered 401 unlinked: deviceId=- kidId=- durable=true reason=unlinked
groups.fix: Often a parent signing the device out on purpose. If nobody did, link the device again and check the storage notice on the dashboard.

groups.layman: The kid device could not check in with the server (Failed to fetch). The child stays signed in and the app keeps trying.
groups.technical: POST /api/kid-session/heartbeat failed: error=Failed to fetch attempt=2 online=false role=kid
groups.fix: Usually a dropped connection or a cold server start. The app retries automatically; fix only if it repeats in the log.

groups.layman: A link code ran out before a parent approved it (ZD41KP). The child's screen shows a fresh code.
groups.technical: pairing expired: code=ZD41KP createdAt=- expiresAt=- approved=false rotated=false
groups.fix: Approve the next code within the time on screen, or raise the pairing window by keeping the link screen open — it now refreshes itself.

groups.layman: This child's device's device was recognised again from its signed cookie, so the child stayed signed in.
groups.technical: device restored from signed backup cookie: deviceId=3d265606-4b84-4be9-9b50-0316df2e7dc1 kidId=12424a8d-773e-4c6c-a885-e7dfd5099b62 storage=unknown durable=false reason=storage had lost the device record
groups.fix: The device link was recovered, but the server storage had lost it. Attach a permanent database (DATABASE_URL) to stop this repeating.

groups.layman: This device cannot read messages out loud, so voice over is switched off here.
groups.technical: speechSynthesis unavailable: userAgent=unknown browser platform=unknown device
groups.fix: Voice over needs a browser with speech support (Chrome, Edge, Safari). Typing still works on this device.

groups.layman: Zoya signed in on This device.
groups.technical: device linked: kidId=68938aab-f980-4432-b397-e296d4ec96cc deviceId=6aa2f391-80da-4c35-8741-6d4f1d6e4c81 label=This device storage=file durable=true
groups.fix: Nothing to do. This is the normal start of a kid session.

groups.layman: The link code on the child's screen was about to run out, so a fresh one appeared automatically.
groups.technical: pairing rotated before expiry: oldCode=YG4TJF newCode=73D6ZK reason=the previous code had expired
groups.fix: Nothing to do. Automatic renewal is what stops the “QR code keeps expiring” problem.

groups.layman: A device asked to be linked and is showing code C2C99V for a parent to approve.
groups.technical: pairing started: code=C2C99V label=This device ttlSeconds=900 expiresAt=2026-10-14T12:31:30.078Z
groups.fix: Nothing to do; this is the normal start of QR linking.
